correctness.rationale: For N≥3, BB^T=(N-2)I+11^T is positive definite and A(J(N,2))=B^TB-2I, yielding distinct Hamiltonian eigenvalues 2(N-2),N-4,-2. For any detector graph X, the unsigned incidence rank is N-b(X) including isolated vertices. The rank on the middle eigenspace is N-b(F)-u(F); on the lowest it is |D|-b(G), and on the trivial sector it is one. Strictly positive losses guarantee precisely the common detector-zero Hamiltonian eigenspaces survive asymptotically. This proves R(D) and the full absorption criterion, while explicit complementary odd-unicyclic constructions meet the bottom eigenspace lower bound for all N≥5; N=3,4 are treated separately. Packaged numerical verifier passed 1760 spectral rank checks, 14 witness/threshold checks, 80 non-Hermitian tests; numerics are corroboration only.

value.rationale: Arbitrary detector placement on a natural infinite family of quantum networks is a meaningful engineering and spectral question. The exact condition identifies which arrangements destroy every dark state through simple bipartite-component/odd-cycle invariants without exponential-state simulation, and the sharp minimum for N≥5 is two below the published generic graph zero-forcing number. The complete classification and sharp, constructive threshold are not merely a routine small case or isolated numerical gain; they explain the structural role of degeneracies and the strict difference between fixed Hamiltonian observability and zero forcing.
